title: Investment Fund Governance for Directors
summary: A ten-module programme giving fund directors the tools to oversee delegates, manage conflicts, protect investors and evidence effective governance to supervisors.
intro: This training programme equips independent directors of investment funds and fund management companies to oversee delegates, manage conflicts, protect investors and evidence effective governance to the authority.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give fund directors a practical grounding in how funds are governed when most activities are delegated, and the tools to oversee the investment manager and other service providers. Participants leave able to set the board's expectations, challenge delegates and management, and evidence sound oversight to supervisors and auditors.
sections.What It Covers: The fund governance model, delegation and oversight of the investment manager, administrator, depositary and distributors, managerial functions and designated persons, conflicts of interest, valuation and liquidity risk management, fees and value for investors, board information and decision-making, regulatory engagement and effectiveness reviews, and emerging issues including AI, ESG and tokenised funds.
Intended Audience: Independent and non-executive directors of investment funds and fund management companies
Executive directors, designated persons and conducting officers of fund management companies
Company secretaries, governance leads and service provider relationship managers supporting fund boards
Learning Objectives: Explain the fund governance model and the board's responsibilities where activities are delegated
Evaluate the oversight of the investment manager, administrator, depositary and distributors
Identify and manage conflicts of interest across the fund and its service providers
Challenge valuation, liquidity, fees and value for investors using structured board questions
Assess the quality of board information, decision-making and engagement with the authority
Anticipate emerging governance issues and agree a board action plan
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two- to three-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the board's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of investment funds or asset management is helpful. No prior board experience is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)

modules.title: The Fund Governance Model
modules.summary: How investment funds and fund management companies are structured and governed, where the board sits among the parties involved, and what fund product and fund manager rules expect of directors.
objectives: Explain the main fund structures and the parties involved in running a fund
Define the duties of fund and management company directors
Distinguish the board's responsibilities from those of its delegates
syllabus: Fund structures: corporate, contractual and partnership vehicles
Self-managed funds, management companies and external fund managers
Directors' duties, independence and acting in investors' best interests
International standards, including the IOSCO principles for collective investment schemes

modules.title: Delegation and Oversight of the Investment Manager
modules.summary: How the board delegates portfolio management while retaining responsibility, and the oversight framework needed to hold the investment manager to account without making investment decisions itself.
objectives: Assess the due diligence and contractual terms underpinning delegation
Evaluate performance, risk and mandate compliance reporting from the investment manager
Challenge the manager while respecting the line between oversight and management
syllabus: Delegation versus abdication: what the board cannot hand over
Initial and ongoing due diligence, mandates and investment restrictions
Performance, risk and breach reporting to the board
Fear of micromanaging: monitoring without directing investment decisions

modules.title: Overseeing the Administrator, Depositary and Distributors
modules.summary: The board's oversight of the fund's other key service providers, from net asset value calculation and safekeeping to distribution and investor onboarding.
objectives: Explain the roles of the administrator, depositary, transfer agent and distributors
Evaluate service levels, controls reports and escalation of errors
Assess distribution oversight, target markets and financial crime controls
syllabus: Administration, transfer agency and NAV error handling
The depositary's independent safekeeping and oversight role
Distribution networks, target market and investor onboarding
Service level agreements, controls reports and on-site reviews

modules.title: Managerial Functions and Designated Persons
modules.summary: How the management company organises its managerial functions, the substance and time commitment the authority expects, and how the board oversees the people who perform them.
objectives: Explain the managerial functions and how they are allocated
Assess substance, resourcing and time commitment of designated persons
Evaluate reporting from designated persons to the board
syllabus: Core managerial functions: investment, risk, distribution, operations and compliance
Allocation, capability and time commitment of designated persons
Substance requirements and avoiding letterbox arrangements
Designated persons' reporting and the board's monitoring plan

modules.title: Conflicts of Interest
modules.summary: Where conflicts arise in fund groups and between the fund, its manager and service providers, and how the board identifies, manages and records them.
objectives: Identify conflicts arising from group structures, fees and related parties
Evaluate the conflicts policy, register and disclosure to investors
Challenge decisions where the manager's interests may differ from investors'
syllabus: Sources of conflict: affiliated service providers, cross-trades and allocation
Directors' own conflicts, multiple directorships and independence
Conflicts policies, registers and board minutes
Case studies of conflicts that harmed investors

modules.title: Valuation and Liquidity Risk Management
modules.summary: The board's oversight of how fund assets are valued and how liquidity is managed, with particular focus on hard-to-value assets and stressed market conditions.
objectives: Assess valuation policies, committees and the treatment of hard-to-value assets
Evaluate liquidity risk management, stress testing and available tools
Challenge management on matching fund liquidity to redemption terms
syllabus: Valuation governance, pricing sources and fair value adjustments
Liquidity mismatch, stress testing and investor concentration
Liquidity management tools: swing pricing, gates and suspensions
Board decisions under stress: lessons from fund suspensions

modules.title: Fees, Costs and Value for Investors
modules.summary: How the board tests whether fees and costs are justified, whether investors receive value, and whether the fund is treating them fairly.
objectives: Explain the components of fund fees and costs
Assess value for investors against performance, service and comparable products
Challenge undue costs and evidence the board's conclusions
syllabus: Management, performance and transaction fees, and other charges
Undue costs and supervisory expectations on fund fees
Value assessment: performance, service, comparable funds and share classes
Fair treatment, disclosure and closet tracking

modules.title: Board Information, Decision-Making and Dynamics
modules.summary: How fund boards can get the right information from delegates, overcome information asymmetry and make well-reasoned decisions, given limited meeting time and a crowded agenda.
objectives: Specify the information the board needs from management and delegates
Evaluate board packs and decision papers for clarity and balance
Apply practical techniques to strengthen challenge and counter group think
syllabus: Agenda overload and prioritising what the board must decide
Information asymmetry between independent directors and the manager
Good decision papers: options, assumptions, downside and recorded rationale
The chair, psychological safety and effective challenge

modules.title: Regulatory Engagement and Board Effectiveness Reviews
modules.summary: What the authority expects to see from fund boards, how to prepare for supervisory engagement, and how to run effectiveness reviews that lead to change.
objectives: Explain supervisory expectations of fund and management company boards
Prepare the board to evidence its oversight to the authority
Evaluate board effectiveness reviews and act on their findings
syllabus: Supervisory thematic reviews of fund governance: recurring findings
Fitness and probity, time commitment and directors' interviews
Board minutes as evidence of challenge and oversight
Effectiveness reviews, skills matrices and succession

modules.title: Emerging Issues: AI, ESG and Tokenised Funds
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a board action plan, examining the governance questions raised by AI, sustainability claims and tokenised fund structures.
objectives: Assess governance risks in the use of AI by managers and service providers
Challenge sustainability claims and the risk of greenwashing
Produce a board action plan for emerging risks
syllabus: AI in portfolio management, risk and operations: board oversight questions
ESG strategies, disclosures and greenwashing risk
Tokenised fund units and distributed ledger infrastructure
Workshop: the fund board's twelve-month oversight plan

related.title: Alternative Investments for Fund Directors
related.summary: An eight-module programme explaining hedge fund, private markets, real asset, structured and digital asset strategies to fund directors, with board questions on valuation, liquidity and fees.

related.title: Board Oversight of Fund Operations and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund directors the tools to oversee fund operations and service providers, from NAV production and custody to errors and resilience.

related.title: Fund Board Governance Toolkit: A Risk-Based Oversight Workshop
related.summary: A six-module practical workshop giving fund directors a risk-based governance toolkit, from skills matrices to escalation triggers, and a draft oversight plan for their own board.

related.title: Overseeing Regulatory Change: Annual Update for Fund Directors
related.summary: A six-module annual CPD update for fund directors on the year's regulatory developments and on overseeing regulatory change and regulatory risk.

related.title: Risk Oversight for Fund and Management Company Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving fund and management company directors the tools to oversee investment, operational and emerging risks and challenge the risk function.

related.title: AI Governance for Boards
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving boards and directors the understanding and tools to govern AI responsibly and evidence sound oversight to regulators.
